newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambia says some camp attackers were Liberian.
newsitem.headline: Gambia says some camp attackers were Liberian.

text.p: The commander of an army camp in Gambia hit by a commando-style raid said on Saturday some of the gunmen may have been Liberians working for a Gambian dissident.
The officer, identified only as Captain Saine, told state television the dawn attack on Farafenni camp in northeast Gambia started when six gunmen overpowered him as he slept.
Gambia said six of its soldiers died. Extra troops helped beat back the attackers, one of whom was captured, while others were held by Senegalese authorities across the border.
"Those people are West Africans," said Saine, who was rescued in the counter-attack.
"The documents found on them show they are Liberians or are working with Kukoi," he said, referring to the leader of Gambia's 1981 abortive coup, Kukoi Samba Sanyang.

Sanyang fled first to Guinea Bissau after Senegalese troops helped put down the uprising. He later went to Libya and then teamed up with Liberia's Charles Taylor who launched civil war in his country in 1989.
Founding president Sir Dawda Jawara, who was the target of the 1981 attempt, was finally overthrown in a 1994 coup led by then Captain Yahya Jammeh, now an elected head of state.
No motive has been advanced publicly for Friday's attack but Farfenni camp is Gambia's second largest military base, located on the only land route to the capital Banjul.

The attackers would have passed through Senegal, whose territory completely surrounds tiny Gambia. The camp is about three km (two miles) from the Senegal border. Authorities have not questioned Senegal's role, instead thanking its government for apprehending the attackers.
Some Gambians speculated the attackers were a mercenary force linked to Jawara, while others raised the possibility of a rebellion. Jawara, exiled in London, has denied involvement.
